questions.question: If 1 January 2018 was a Monday, then what day was it on 1 January 2019?
questions.solution:
As 2018 was not a leap year, next year the same date will come on 1 day after the preceding year's day.

The no.of odd days in ordinary year is 1 odd day 

**1 ordinary year = 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day.**

As on 1 January, 2018 it was Monday, on 1 January, 2019 it will be Monday + 1 odd day which was Tuesday.

**Hence on 1 January, 2019 it was Tuesday.**

Thus, the correct answer is 'Tuesday'.

questions.question: Which Mughal structure is renowned for its pietra dura inlay work using semi-precious stones on white marble?

__
 
• The Taj Mahal, located in Agra, India, is globally renowned for its intricate **pietra dura inlay work**, which involves embedding semi-precious stones into white marble.
 
• It was commissioned by **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan** in 1632 as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal and completed in 1648.
 
• The semi-precious stones used in the inlay work include lapis lazuli, jade, turquoise, and agate, creating floral and geometric patterns.
 
• This architectural masterpiece is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and represents the pinnacle of Mughal architecture, blending Persian, Islamic, and Indian design elements.
 
• The Taj Mahal is considered a symbol of eternal love and attracts millions of visitors annually due to its exquisite beauty and craftsmanship.

• It is built using red sandstone and features a combination of Islamic and Hindu architectural styles.
 
• Structures within the fort include the Jahangir Mahal, Khas Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, and the Diwan-i-Am.
 
• Though known for its robust construction and historical significance, it does not feature pietra dura work.

• It was built by Shah Jahan in 1648 and served as the political and ceremonial center of the Mughal Empire.
 
• The fort is primarily constructed using red sandstone and is known for its architectural brilliance, including the Lahori Gate and Rang Mahal.
 
• However, it does not exhibit the intricate pietra dura work found in the Taj Mahal.

• The site is famous for its architectural marvels such as the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, and Panch Mahal.
 
• It is constructed using red sandstone and reflects the fusion of Mughal and Hindu architectural styles.
 
• Unlike the Taj Mahal, it does not feature pietra dura inlay work.

questions.question: In boxing, the abbreviation “TKO” refers to a specific decision when a referee stops the match. What does it stand for for?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Technical Knockout'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Technical Knockout (TKO):**
 
 
• A Technical Knockout (TKO) is a term used in combat sports, such as boxing and mixed martial arts, to describe a stoppage by the referee.
 
• It occurs when the referee determines that a fighter cannot safely continue the match, even if they have not been knocked unconscious.
 
• The decision is typically made when a fighter is taking excessive punishment, is unable to intelligently defend themselves, or has sustained a serious injury (like a severe cut).
 
• Unlike a standard Knockout (KO), where a fighter fails to stand up before the referee's count of ten, a TKO is a proactive measure taken to ensure the athlete's long-term health and safety.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technical Keep Out:**
 
 
• This is an incorrect term and does not exist in the official rules or terminology of boxing or any recognized combat sport.
 
• It is likely used as a distractor because it shares the same first word as the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Total Knockout:**
 
 
• While "Total" might imply a complete defeat, it is not the official technical term used by boxing commissions or governing bodies.
 
• The term "Technical" is preferred because the stoppage is based on a technical assessment of the fighter's condition rather than a physical failure to beat a count.
 
 
 
• **Time Knockout:**
 
 
• This is not a recognized term in professional boxing. While time is vital in boxing (rounds, 10-counts, and rest periods), it is never used to define a referee's stoppage decision.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A TKO can also be declared if a **ringside physician** determines the fighter is unfit to continue due to injury.
 
• If a fighter's corner "throws in the towel" to stop the fight, it is also officially recorded as a **Technical Knockout**.
 
• In some boxing jurisdictions, the **"Three-Knockdown Rule"** is in effect, where three knockdowns in a single round result in an automatic TKO.
 
• The primary objective of a TKO is **injury prevention**, specifically to avoid unnecessary brain trauma when a fighter is clearly outmatched.
</ul

questions.question: Who was the Governor General of Bengal when the Permanent Settlement was introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Cornwallis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Charles Cornwallis**, the Governor-General of Bengal from 1786 to 1793, introduced the **Permanent Settlement** in 1793.
 
• The Permanent Settlement was primarily implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to stabilize revenue collection and establish a class of loyal landlords.
 
• Under this system, zamindars (landlords) were recognized as the owners of land and were responsible for collecting taxes from farmers.
 
• The revenue to be paid by the zamindars to the British government was fixed permanently, hence the term **Permanent Settlement**.
 
• Cornwallis believed that a fixed revenue system would ensure stability, reduce corruption, and encourage zamindars to invest in improving agricultural productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System:**

 
 
• The zamindars became intermediaries between the British government and the farmers, collecting taxes on behalf of the government.
 
• While the system aimed to ensure steady revenue, it often led to exploitation of farmers by zamindars.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Permanent Settlement:**
 
 
• It created a class of wealthy zamindars who wielded significant influence in rural areas.
 
• Farmers were often burdened by high taxes, leading to widespread poverty and indebtedness.
 
• The rigidity of fixed revenue created challenges during famines and poor harvests.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• The system failed to account for changes in agricultural productivity and economic conditions.
 
• The British government suffered revenue losses when agricultural output increased, as the tax amount remained unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Other Land Revenue Systems:**
 
 
• Besides Permanent Settlement, the British introduced other systems such as the **Ryotwari** and **Mahalwari** systems to manage land revenue in different regions of India.
 
• Ryotwari system was implemented in Madras and Bombay Presidencies, where farmers directly paid taxes to the government.
 
• Mahalwari system, prevalent in North India, involved collective revenue payments by villages.

questions.question: A trader sells wheat at 20% profit and uses 20% less than the actual measure. His gain % is?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for **total gain percentage** in dishonest dealing:

**Net Gain %** = [ {(100 + %Profit) ÷ (100 − %Less Weight)} − 1 ] × 100

⇒ Net Gain % = [ {(100 + 20) ÷ (100 − 20)} − 1 ] × 100

⇒ Net Gain % = [ {120 ÷ 80} − 1 ] × 100 = [ 1.5 − 1 ] × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Claimed **Profit Percentage** = 20%

**Weight Reduction** = 20%

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1000 g of wheat be ₹1000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b06a1a23ff87592cc855f02b368fa7cbc566015af3b2007cb3e148d09608e49.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of the weight actually sold (800 g) = ₹800

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** charged by the trader = CP of 1000 g + 20% of CP = 1000 + 200 = ₹1200

⇒ **Total Profit** = SP − Actual CP = 1200 − 800 = ₹400

⇒ **Gain Percentage** = (Total Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (400 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 1/2 × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

A dealer makes a profit by either marking up the **Cost Price** or using **false weights**. If both are done, the net profit is calculated on the actual cost of the goods delivered.

Profit with False Weight Only

If a dealer sells at cost price but uses a weight of **w** instead of **W**, then Gain % = [(W − w) ÷ w] × 100.

Successive Profit Formula

Net Profit % = [{(100 + P₁) × (100 + P₂) ÷ 100²} − 1] × 100, where P₁ is price profit and P₂ is weight-based profit.

In ΔABC, AB = 9 cm, AC = 7 cm, and BC = 12 cm. The length of median AD is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using **Apollonius's Theorem** for triangle ABC with median AD:

AB² + AC² = 2 × (AD² + BD²)

Substitute the values: 9² + 7² = 2 × (AD² + 6²)

⇒ 81 + 49 = 2 × (AD² + 36)

⇒ 130 = 2 × (AD² + 36)

⇒ 65 = AD² + 36 ⇒ AD² = 29

⇒ AD = √29 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √29 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In **ΔABC**, **AB = 9 cm**, **AC = 7 cm**, and **BC = 12 cm**. **AD** is the **median** to side **BC**.

**Formula Used:** **Apollonius's Theorem** states that the sum of the squares of any two sides of a triangle is equal to twice the sum of the square of half the third side and the square of the median bisecting the third side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b8c56dd0000c1dc742a6db6e1c5356d19585c3bd7cf6dbe9dbafa69377e3a9e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **AD** is the **median**, **D** is the **midpoint** of **BC**.

⇒ **BD = CD = BC ÷ 2** = 12 ÷ 2 = **6 cm**

⇒ Applying **Apollonius's Theorem**: AB² + AC² = 2(AD² + BD²)

⇒ 9² + 7² = 2(AD² + 6²)

⇒ 81 + 49 = 2(AD² + 36)

⇒ 130 = 2(AD² + 36)

⇒ 130 ÷ 2 = AD² + 36

⇒ 65 = AD² + 36

⇒ AD² = 65 − 36 = 29

⇒ AD = √29 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √29 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Apollonius's Theorem

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the interests on Rs. 50,000 for one year at 8% per annum compounded half yearly and yearly?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate for half-yearly compounding = 8% ÷ 2 = 4%.

Number of periods for 1 year = 2.

Effective rate for 2 periods at 4% = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

Rate for yearly compounding = 8.00%.

Difference in interest = (8.16% − 8.00%) of ₹50,000 = 0.16% of 50,000.

Difference = (0.16 / 100) × 50,000 = 0.16 × 500 = ₹80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹50,000, Rate (R) = 8% p.a., Time (T) = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Compound Interest (CI) = P[(1 + r/n)ⁿt − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15f39c496eafc841a0d3c3fa61e3b2afb0af4c2baed8073e2156133cf61b4ce8.png] 

Case 1: Interest compounded yearly for 1 year

⇒ CIyₑₐᵣₗy = (50,000 × 8 × 1) / 100 = ₹4,000.

Case 2: Interest compounded half-yearly for 1 year

⇒ Rate (r) = 8% / 2 = 4% per half-year.

⇒ Time (n) = 2 half-years.

⇒ Amount (A) = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ A = 50,000 × (1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 50,000 × (1.04)²

⇒ A = 50,000 × 1.0816 = ₹54,080.

⇒ CIₕₐₗf₋yₑₐᵣₗy = Amount − Principal = 54,080 − 50,000 = ₹4,080.

Difference Calculation:

⇒ Difference = CIₕₐₗf₋yₑₐᵣₗy − CIyₑₐᵣₗy

⇒ Difference = 4,080 − 4,000 = ₹80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Periods

The difference between CI and SI for two conversion periods is given by the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)². In this question, one year compounded half-yearly effectively acts as two periods.

Successive Percentage Change

The effective rate for two compounding periods can be calculated using the formula: x + y + (xy/100), where x and y are the rates for each period.

Compounding Frequencies

If interest is compounded 'n' times a year, the nominal annual rate R is divided by n, and the total time T is multiplied by n to calculate the interest.

questions.question: If b cos θ = a, then cosecθ + cotθ = _________.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **half-angle identity**: cosec θ + cot θ = √((1 + cos θ) / (1 − cos θ)).

Given: b cos θ = a → **cos θ = a/b**.

Substitute cos θ in the formula: √((1 + a/b) / (1 − a/b)).

Simplify the fraction: √(((b + a)/b) / ((b − a)/b)) = √((b + a) / (b − a)).

**∴ The correct answer is √(b+a)/(b-a).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** b cos θ = a ⇒ cos θ = a/b

In a **right-angled triangle**, cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed6415f16d39db043e3316bbcce46ce46266e29b555362ef623ddb4e6513dec3.png] 

⇒ By **Pythagoras Theorem**: Perpendicular = √(Hypotenuse² − Base²) = √(b² − a²).

⇒ sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = √(b² − a²) / b

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = (1 / sin θ) + (cos θ / sin θ) = (1 + cos θ) / sin θ

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = (1 + a/b) / (√(b² − a²) / b)

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = ((b + a) / b) × (b / √(b² − a²))

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = (b + a) / √((b + a)(b − a))

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ = √(b + a) / √(b − a) = √((b + a) / (b − a))

**∴ The correct answer is √(b+a)/(b-a).**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identity

The relation **cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1** can be factored as (cosecθ − cotθ)(cosecθ + cotθ) = 1.

Reciprocal Relation

**cosec θ + cot θ** is the reciprocal of **cosec θ − cot θ**.

Half-Angle Formula

The expression **cosec θ + cot θ** is always equal to **cot(θ/2)**.

Pythagorean Triplet

For any right triangle with sides x, y and hypotenuse z, **x² + y² = z²**.</p

**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

She exclaimed that the flowers were lovely.

options.text: She said, "How lovely the flowers are!"
She said that the flowers are lovely

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The given sentence is in **indirect speech**. The **conversion to direct speech **is given in option** (1)**.

__**While converting from indirect to Direct speech, the following changes/rules must be taken into consideration:**__

 
• Quotation marks are added and the sentence ends with a full stop, comma or interrogation mark depending on the tone of the reported speech.
 
• The tense of the verb, in the reported speech involving any order, request and instruction does not undergo any change during the conversion from indirect to direct mode. This is also true if the statement is a universal truth.
 
• If the reporting verb is in the present tense, it does not undergo any change.
 
• We omit the word 'to' before the verb if the verb is in bare infinitive.
 
• When the reporting or principal verb is in the past tense, all past tenses of the indirect are changed into the corresponding present tenses.
 
• Words expressing distance are generally converted into words expressing nearness in time or place. For eg. then becomes now, that day becomes today, that becomes this etc.
 
• In reporting commands and requests, the verb expressing command or request is omitted and the infinitive is changed into the imperative.
 
• In reporting questions the verbs like asked, inquired are omitted and replaced by 'said to'.
 
• In reporting exclamations and wishes, the verb expressing exclamation or wish is omitted and simply replaced by 'said'

Option 1 follows all the rules correctly. Other options are incorrect.
